answer: The forge test I would run is Goodreads reading history: books logged and rated over years, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. Each account presents its proof once, the network verifies it in seconds, and a farm that wants ten accounts must pass ten independent checks — the umber is that the work cannot be shared or replayed. Scale is the enemy of the attacker here. The vertex grows with every clone, but the reward per clone stays fixed, so the farm goes broke before it goes big.
